Glucagon-secreting endocrine pancreatic tumor; necrolytic skin lesions, anemia, and glossitis/stomatitis each occur in 30-79%. Thromboembolism is below 30%.
Severe osteochondrodysplasia affecting long bones, vertebrae and ribs. Other listed anomalies lack established common functional organ damage.

Ataxia, sensorineural deafness and cardiomyopathy define the syndrome. Unspecified skin abnormality does not establish damaging involvement.
Malignant tumor located in the rectum; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle organ involvement.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with azoospermia and infertility; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Lipid-storage histiocytosis involving marrow and spleen with thrombocytopenia. Liver enzyme elevations in one patient do not establish common liver damage; cirrhosis is a minority feature.

N-linked glycosylation disorder defined by intellectual disability and developmental delay, each in 80-99%. Skin laxity and skeletal damage are not established as common.
Congenital cardiac outflow malformation with ventricular septal defect.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia with long-bone deformities and exostoses. Premature tooth loss occurs in only 5-29%.
Benign neoplasm of the pituitary endocrine gland. Neurologic or visual damage is not established across this umbrella.
Inherited superficial epidermal fragility causing generalized or acral erosions; no common extracutaneous damage established.
Subcutaneous fat loss with severe metabolic dysfunction; phalangeal osteolysis in 30-79%. Steatosis and atherosclerosis are separately diagnosed complications.
Metastatic tumor directly occupies the spinal cord. The unspecified original tumor site supplies no additional axis.
Neurodevelopmental disease, mesomelic dysplasia and renal malformations define the syndrome; strabismus in 7/18 (39%). Hypertrichosis is non-damaging; constipation alone adds no organ.
CNS malformation and intellectual disability define the disease; muscle atrophy and strabismus each in 80-99%, with myopathy in 30-79%. Feeding difficulty alone adds no GI damage.
Hypoglycin intoxication directly disrupts energy metabolism and gluconeogenesis, causing toxic hypoglycemia. Vomiting alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Meningeal tumor specifically involving the pituitary stalk, an endocrine structure; no additional common organ damage established.
